name: ACE-031

lead: ACE-031 is a lab-made decoy receptor that soaks up myostatin and related proteins that restrain muscle growth. Muscle-focused forum users cite it as a route to a fuller physique beyond natural limits.

It fuses the activin receptor IIB to an antibody Fc piece and binds myostatin and related ligands in the blood so they cannot signal in muscle. With less brake on growth, muscle mass rises. It was tested in healthy postmenopausal women and in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, where it raised muscle measures; its use in healthy lifters has not been studied.

paras: It was used only in clinical trials, which have ended. Anti-doping scientists have published detection methods for black-market versions, showing athletes outside clinics have shown interest.
The healthy-volunteer study reported it generally well tolerated, with injection-site reactions. The Duchenne trials were terminated, and it is not approved anywhere.

angle.text: ACE-031 is a myostatin-blocking decoy protein that removes the body's brake on muscle growth to build a fuller physique. It raised muscle measures in healthy women and Duchenne boys. The trials have ended and it is not approved.

lead: ACE-031 is a soluble fusion protein made from the activin receptor type IIB (ActRIIB) and the Fc portion of human IgG1. Acting as a decoy receptor, it binds myostatin (GDF-8) and related proteins that restrain muscle growth, so less of them reaches the receptors on muscle cells [1][2][3]. The goal of that design is more lean mass and strength, which is the reason strength-sport communities follow it as a route to a more muscular physique.

It was developed for muscle-wasting conditions and tested in healthy postmenopausal women and in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy [1][2][4]. In the healthy-volunteer study, a single dose was followed by measurable gains in lean body mass and thigh muscle volume at four weeks [2]. The Duchenne trials were stopped, and the compound is not approved anywhere [1][4].

Interest outside clinics is visible in two places: bodybuilding forums such as T Nation, where members discussed it as an upcoming myostatin blocker from 2008 onward [5][6], and in anti-doping science, where reviews list ACE-031 among emerging muscle-regulating drugs and chemists have published methods for detecting black-market material [7][8].

sections.h: Background: myostatin and the activin pathway
paras: Myostatin is a protein in the TGF-beta family, made mainly in skeletal muscle, that limits how much muscle forms. Mice lacking the gene, reported by Se-Jin Lee and Alexandra McPherron in 1997, had roughly twice the normal muscle mass and were nicknamed mighty mice. The same year, mutations in the myostatin gene were identified in double-muscled Belgian Blue and Piedmontese cattle. A German boy with mutations in both gene copies, described in 2004, was reported to be unusually strong for his age [9].

Myostatin signals through activin receptor type IIB, and other ligands such as activin A use the same receptor. A soluble version of that receptor can therefore soak up several growth-limiting ligands at once, rather than myostatin alone [2][10]. Wikipedia's myostatin article records that a soluble activin IIB receptor raised muscle mass in mice by up to 60% over two weeks in 2005 work, and that an antibody against myostatin (stamulumab, MYO-029) was dropped by Wyeth for muscular dystrophy in 2008 [9].

By binding myostatin (GDF-8) and other negative regulators, ACE-031 reduces their signalling through native receptors [2][3]. In mice, 28 days of treatment increased muscle mass independent of fibre type, unlike selective myostatin inhibition, which was reported to act mainly on type II fibres [10]. In the healthy-volunteer study, serum biomarkers also moved in directions the authors interpreted as changes in bone and fat metabolism [2].

After a single subcutaneous dose in 48 healthy postmenopausal women, exposure rose linearly with dose and the mean half-life was 10 to 15 days, long enough that dosing intervals of two to four weeks were used in the Duchenne trial [1][2].

A single ascending-dose study in 48 healthy postmenopausal women (0.02-3 mg/kg subcutaneously versus placebo, 3:1) found ACE-031 generally well tolerated, with injection-site erythema among reported adverse events. At day 29 in the 3 mg/kg group, total body lean mass was 3.3% higher by DXA and thigh muscle volume 5.1% higher by MRI [2]. A second phase 1 study in 70 healthy postmenopausal women was also registered [11], and a first phase 1 listing began in September 2008 [12].

A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, ascending-dose trial in ambulatory boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy had safety as its primary objective, with doses given every two to four weeks. No serious or severe adverse events were reported, but the study was stopped after the second dosing regimen because of potential safety concerns of nosebleeds (epistaxis) and dilated small blood vessels (telangiectasias). The ACE-031 groups showed non-significant trends toward maintained six-minute walk distance, against a decline on placebo, and toward higher lean mass, bone mineral density and lower fat mass [1]. The phase 2 trial enrolled 24 participants and its extension 11 before both were terminated [4][13].

Preclinical work includes a 2025-2026 study reporting increased muscle mass and strength in common marmosets, a primate model [14][15]. Related ActRIIB-Fc proteins have been studied in mouse models of cancer and chemotherapy-induced muscle loss, heart failure and heart attack injury, where they preserved muscle in some and protected the heart in others [16][17][18].

Reported effects in humans are injection-site erythema in healthy women and nosebleeds and telangiectasias in boys with Duchenne, the latter prompting the early end of that trial; the authors described these as non-muscle-related adverse events [1][2]. Forum members discussing myostatin inhibitors have raised questions about long-term safety and the lack of human data in athletes [6].

Anti-doping reviews list emerging muscle-regulating drugs such as ACE-031 as potential targets for misuse by athletes [7]. Wikipedia's myostatin article notes that the World Anti-Doping Agency bans myostatin inhibitors, and that counterfeit myostatin blockers were being sold online by 2012 [9]. A 2025 paper described a gel-electrophoretic method for detecting black-market ACE-031 [8].

On T Nation, a 2008 thread described ACE-031 as the newest anabolic substance, a myostatin binder that would let muscle grow uninhibited [5]. A 2011 thread titled around ACVR2B (ACE-031) discussed claims that a human myostatin blocker was near [19], and threads in 2013 asked whether myostatin inhibitors such as follistatin, ACE-031 and MYO-029 might harm health and whether members would try them given sparse data [6][20].

lore.intro: ACE-031 is discussed on strength-training forums as a myostatin blocker that could allow muscle growth beyond usual limits [5][19].

claims.claim: Myostatin inhibitors are safe enough to try.
